items.title: HHS adds new IDR entity as surprise billing disputes surge
items.reason: This item directly addresses IDR process implementation under the No Surprises Act, specifically the addition of a new certified dispute resolution entity, which is a material development in the federal framework affecting revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: HHS has certified Physio Solutions (operating as Medlitix) as the 17th Independent Dispute Resolution entity authorized to arbitrate out-of-network payment disputes under the No Surprises Act. This expansion comes as IDR dispute volumes surge and the program faces increased scrutiny from researchers and lawmakers regarding arbiter performance and fairness. The addition of new IDR entities directly affects how healthcare revenue-cycle teams will process and resolve surprise billing disputes, as the growing network of certified arbiters may impact resolution timelines and outcomes for out-of-network claim disputes.

items.title: Judge dismisses Ballad Health's MA claims denial lawsuit against UnitedHealth
items.reason: This reports a judicial ruling (dismissal) in a provider lawsuit against a major payer (UnitedHealthcare) involving Medicare Advantage claims denials, which is directly within the scope of payer litigation and enforcement.
items.summary: A federal court dismissed Ballad Health's lawsuit against UnitedHealthcare alleging routine denial or delay of Medicare Advantage claims deemed medically necessary by physicians. The court ordered the dispute into arbitration, where Ballad Health indicated it will continue pursuing the matter. This case addresses a core revenue-cycle concern for providers: payer claims-denial practices in the MA space and the procedural mechanisms (arbitration vs. litigation) available to challenge them.
